method: Independent direct HTTP status, redirect, media-type, byte-length and content-hash checks; page-level review of the Tiger investment and CSP PDFs; direct SEC, Tiger, OIC and transaction-source review for entry, current involvement, retained operating perimeter and the 2023 retail divestiture

verifiedClaims: Tiger announced the closing of an investment in Cleopatra Resources LLC on May 28, 2015
Transaction terms were not disclosed
The company was established in 2011 and developed American Natural multi-fuel stations across Pennsylvania and Ohio
Tiger explicitly described the company as CNG energy infrastructure and described itself as an infrastructure investor
American Natural Supply acquired the key business assets of Satterlee on December 7, 2017
Tiger led a concurrent parent-level equity investment and Orion provided financing to ANS
ANS operated a terminal and related-infrastructure network serving commercial and energy-sector customers
In 2018 the retail chain comprised 13 convenience stores: two American Natural Energy Centres and eleven conventional gasoline-branded stores
Jennifer Pomerantz founded Cleopatra Resources in 2011 to launch American Natural

sources.verificationMethod: Direct SEC filing was independently indexed and opened in the research browser despite SEC rate limiting the curl verifier
verifiedClaims: Cleopatra Resources made a Rule 506(c) equity offering with a first sale on April 22, 2022
The filing reported a $25 million offering, $10 million sold and one investor
The filing does not identify the investor or disclose the resulting ownership percentage or control
Cleopatra sold substantially all convenience-retail assets of American Natural Retail PA LLC to Giant Oil in December 2023
The transaction included eleven operating convenience stores and two additional retail locations scheduled for transaction closing in 2024
The announcement concerned the retail subsidiary and did not state that retained ANS wholesale operations were sold
Tiger General Counsel Danielle Hunt currently serves on the board of American Natural
Tiger Operating Partner Jonathan O'Donnell is identified as a recent American Natural CFO and describes American Natural as a Tiger portfolio company
OIC currently presents American Natural Supply as an unrealized 2017 investment
OIC describes ANS as a Pittsburgh commercial fuel-supply and storage company with terminals and related infrastructure serving commercial, industrial and energy customers
OIC's unrealized status describes OIC's own position and does not establish Tiger's ownership percentage
Tiger continues to publish American Natural with a 2015 initial investment, Energy Transition sector and North America geography
The page's operating copy still includes divested retail activity and therefore cannot define the current company perimeter by itself

exitSearch.result: The December 2023 sale removed substantially all convenience-retail assets, but no sale of the retained ANS wholesale fuel-supply and storage business or full Tiger exit was found. Current Tiger board representation and its live portfolio listing support continuing involvement. OIC independently continues to list ANS as unrealized.

responseSourceHealthCorrections: Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund I and sole ownership are not directly disclosed by the reviewed primary sources; fund, vehicle, security, stake and full cap table remain NOT_PUBLICLY_DISCLOSED.
The 2022 Form D proves an equity sale to one investor but does not identify the investor or establish the effect on Tiger's percentage or control.
OIC's unrealized status confirms ANS continuity and OIC's own position; it is not treated as proof of Tiger's stake.
The two additional retail locations in the 2023 announcement were scheduled for transaction closing in 2024; they are not described as store closures.
Tiger's live portfolio copy is stale because it still describes retail operations sold to Giant, so the retained company boundary is ANS fuel supply, storage, terminals and logistics.
